newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli indicators show growing economic activity.
newsitem.headline: Israeli indicators show growing economic activity.

text.p: Preliminary Israeli indicators through October show increased economic activity, despite a slowdown in consumer spending, the Central Bureau of Statistics said on Wednesday.

The bureau said imports of capital goods rose in August-September after remaining stable for the April-July period. The industrial production index rose at a 5-6 percent annualised rate in July-September, compared with a 3-4 percent pace in March-June.
In addition, the bureau said it found that industrial exports, discounting diamonds and exports to the West Bank and Gaza, renewed their growth from May after stabilising in February-April.
Merchandise exports, the bureau said, grew at an annualised pace of 20 percent in October, compared with 18 percent in September and 14 percent in August.

The bureau noted, however, that preliminary indicators for consumer spending showed a decline. Revenues from value-added tax and customs were unchanged or declined in recent months, while retail sales have shown almost no change since August.

It said inflation had slowed since May to an annualised rate of just four percent in October. The shekel lost an annualised 10 percent against the official basket of foreign currencies in September-October, after gaining in July-August, the bureau said.
